edits.new: The Atlas Infinite public-preview overview excludes Atlas Kubernetes Operator support, and the Operator changelog repeats that the Operator doesn't support Atlas Infinite clusters in public preview. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/infinite/atlas-infinite-landing/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/operator/current/ak8so-changelog.md

statements.statement: The public-preview overview excludes Atlas Kubernetes Operator.
statements.note: Stated on the landing page and in the Operator changelog.

statements.statement: The generated Operator API documentation contains databaseEdition=INFINITE and Infinite-specific storage fields.
statements.note: Searches did not surface any Operator CRD or API doc with a databaseEdition field or an INFINITE value.

queries: AtlasDeployment CRD databaseEdition INFINITE storage mongodb-atlas-kubernetes

statements.statement: Schema presence alone does not establish supported Operator operation.
statements.note: Interpretive caveat. The docs do say the Operator does not support Infinite clusters in public preview.

queries: AtlasDeployment CRD databaseEdition INFINITE storage mongodb-atlas-kubernetes

edits.rationale: The exclusion is confirmed by both the Infinite landing page and the Atlas Kubernetes Operator changelog. I found no source for the statement that generated Operator API docs contain databaseEdition=INFINITE and Infinite-specific storage fields, so it is dropped. The caveat that schema presence does not establish support is editorial reasoning, not a checkable fact.

edits.old: ByteDiagram independently frames tier-bound IOPS as an architecture-review pitfall, and The Weighted Average distinguishes published throughput specifications from application measurements. Both derive product facts from MongoDB material; they are separate editorial analyses, not independent verification of vendor limits. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-30)
edits.new: ByteDiagram frames tier-bound IOPS as an architecture pitfall: storage size can grow, but storage performance follows the cluster tier tables, and the docs publish fixed IOPS/MBps tables per tier. This is a secondary editorial analysis, not independent verification of vendor limits. Sources: https://bytediagram.com/blog/mongodb-atlas-infinite-architecture-diagram.html

evidence.quote: IOPS still tier-bound — storage size can grow, but storage performance follows the cluster tier tables; changing IOPS means changing tier.
Storage IOPS and throughput are tied to the chosen cluster tier (docs publish fixed IOPS/MBps tables per tier)
